findings.title: Org-scope authorization silently skips direct org members when there are no child teams
findings.body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the user membership lookup is gated on `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`, even though `teamIds` always contains the org's own ID (`[options.orgId, ...teamsFromOrg.map(t => t.id)]`). When an organization has zero child teams but has direct members (a realistic configuration, e.g., a small org that hasn't created sub-teams), `userIdsFromOrg` is forced to an empty array. As a result, personal (non-team) bookings made by those direct org members will not match the authorization SQL: the first branch only matches `isTeamBooking = true`, and the second branch is excluded entirely. Those users effectively disappear from org-scope insights. The user lookup should be performed whenever `teamIds` is non-empty, not based on `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`. The PR is the right moment to fix this since the file is being rewritten anyway; preserving the bug in raw SQL form just locks it in.

findings.title: `findMany` removed without documenting the migration for external callers
findings.body: The class previously exposed `async findMany(findManyArgs)`, which built a Prisma `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` query using the constructed auth/filter conditions. That method is gone and has been replaced with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`, forcing every caller to switch to `prisma.$queryRaw` and to hand-write the SELECT clause themselves. This is a breaking change for any in-repo caller that imports `InsightsBookingService` (the file is in `packages/lib/server/service`, which is a shared library package). The PR description only discusses the test changes and does not call out this API break or describe the migration. A grep for `InsightsBookingService` consumers should be done and they should be updated in the same change, or at minimum the PR description should list them.

findings.title: Caching tests removed with no replacement
findings.body: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching", ...)` block (two tests: "should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") without adding equivalent coverage. The implementation still caches via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` (lines 84 and 91 in `insightsBooking.ts`), so a future refactor that accidentally re-builds conditions on every call (e.g., removing the `=== undefined` guard) would not be caught. At minimum one test should be added that asserts a second call returns the exact same `Prisma.Sql` instance / deep-equal structure as the first.

findings.title: Tests have not been executed for a HIGH RISK SQL/authorization PR
findings.body: The PR description itself states that the author "encountered test runner configuration issues" and explicitly asks reviewers to manually run `TZ=UTC yarn test packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts`. For a change that the author flags as HIGH RISK and that touches authorization conditions built with `Prisma.sql` template literals, this is not acceptable. Several non-obvious things need to actually execute and return correct rows: (a) JS arrays interpolated into `Prisma.sql` are correctly serialized for PostgreSQL `ANY()` (see line 296 for the single-element case and lines 333-342 for the multi-element case — if Prisma emits them as `'{}'` or as a comma list rather than a proper array, the query fails); (b) the `(isTeamBooking = true)` / `(isTeamBooking = false)` predicates produce correct row matching against the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table; (c) the cached conditions actually short-circuit; (d) the org-scope test's expected array order matches the order returned by `findAllByParentId`. None of this has been verified by the author. The merge should be blocked until CI proves these tests pass against a populated database.
